Method

Late steering-vector fusion

A direction-agnostic front end computes mixture features once. A parameter-shared beamforming head combines these features with each requested steering direction to estimate target-specific spatial weights.

Multichannel mixtureSix microphone signals
→
Shared feature extractorOne evaluation per mixture
→
ABeamforming head+ steering vector A
BSame head parameters+ steering vector B
→
Target ATarget B

The front-end representation is reused across targets. The head is evaluated separately for each requested direction.

Computational complexity and delay

Matched Lightweight models

Early fusion makes most computation target dependent. Late fusion reuses the front end and evaluates a smaller target-specific path for each requested direction.

Three requested targets, 10 ms input packets, and one CPU thread.

Output delay includes buffering, computation, and scheduling. Processing P95 is measured separately; percentiles are not additive.

Runtime protocol +

Intel Core i9-10900; one pinned logical CPU; one intra-operation and one inter-operation thread. Offline RTF: batch size one, a 1-second six-channel input, 10 warm-ups, and the median of 40 timed runs. Streaming: a warm-loaded stateful pipeline with causal gain estimation, three paced replays of one 10-second recording. The median of the three per-trial P95 delays is reported. File/model loading, DOA estimation, and audio-device/ADC/DAC buffers are excluded. These timings are independent of the prerecorded listening outputs above.

Full-test results

Original two-source test set

Across 370 original two-source test configurations and four nominal array SNRs, matched Late fusion improves mean SI-SDR over Early fusion.

Closely spaced sources remain challenging: mean SI-SDR is negative at 10° separation. Late fusion does not lead every quality metric.

370 acoustic configurations · 0 / 5 / 10 / 15 dB array SNR

Array SNR compares summed fully reverberant speech with additive noise, averaged over time and all six microphones. It is not a fixed per-target TNR.
